CVE-2016-2183.name: Sweet32 Birthday Attack on 64-bit Block Ciphers (3DES/Blowfish)
CVE-2016-2183.description: Legacy 64-bit block ciphers are vulnerable to birthday attacks after capturing approximately 32 GB of data within a single session, enabling plaintext recovery.

CVE-2015-4000.name: Logjam Attack on Weak Diffie-Hellman Groups (<2048-bit)
CVE-2015-4000.description: Diffie-Hellman key exchanges using groups with 1024 bits or fewer can be precomputed and cracked by sophisticated adversaries, compromising session keys.
CVE-2015-4000.remediation: Enforce DH Group 14 (2048-bit MODP), Group 19 (256-bit ECP), or Group 20 (384-bit ECP).

CVE-1999-0524.name: IKEv1 Aggressive Mode Pre-Shared Key Hash Leakage
CVE-1999-0524.description: IKEv1 Aggressive Mode transmits authentication hashes containing the Pre-Shared Key in cleartext, allowing offline dictionary and brute-force cracking.
CVE-1999-0524.remediation: Migrate from IKEv1 to IKEv2 or use IKEv1 Main Mode with digital certificates instead of PSK.

REPLAY-ATTACK-001.name: Disabled Replay Protection or Missing Extended Sequence Numbers (ESN)
REPLAY-ATTACK-001.description: If replay protection is disabled or standard 32-bit sequence numbers wrap around on high-throughput links without ESN (RFC 4303), attackers can replay captured ESP packets.
REPLAY-ATTACK-001.remediation: Enable anti-replay window (minimum 64 packets) and configure Extended Sequence Numbers (ESN).

NO-PFS-001.name: Perfect Forward Secrecy (PFS) Disabled
NO-PFS-001.description: Without PFS, Phase 2 child SAs derive encryption keys directly from Phase 1 master keys. Compromise of the long-term Phase 1 key allows retroactive decryption of all historical IPsec traffic.
NO-PFS-001.remediation: Enable PFS (pfs=yes / esp_dh_group) to mandate a new Diffie-Hellman exchange for each child SA.

MD5-SHA1-COLLISION.name: Use of Collision-Prone Hash Functions (MD5 / SHA-1)
MD5-SHA1-COLLISION.description: MD5 and SHA-1 suffer from demonstrated practical cryptographic collision attacks. Their usage in integrity authentication undermines SA integrity verification.
MD5-SHA1-COLLISION.remediation: Upgrade integrity transforms to HMAC-SHA256, HMAC-SHA384, or use AEAD ciphers (AES-GCM).
